chunks: And from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
One who relieves a distress from his Muslim brother, Allah will remove a distress from him on the Day of Resurrection, and he shall come forth from his grave with a delighted chest.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a Muslim brother in distress?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the reciprocal nature of divine mercy, where alleviating a believer's worldly distress guarantees relief from the anxieties of the Hereafter. The specific mention of emerging from the grave 'like the chest is wide' (mujallaj al-sadr) alludes to the removal of spiritual constriction and anxiety, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the state of the righteous on Judgment Day. This hadith underscores the practical spirituality of social support as a means of securing personal eschatological peace.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 121. It has been related that al-Sadiq (a.s) said:
One who relieves a distress from his Muslim brother, Allah will remove a distress from him on the Day of Resurrection and he shall come forth from his grave delighted.
